question.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}-17{x}_{2}^{2}+7{x}_{3}^{2}-18{x}_{2}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
question.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -17 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-20)I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -17 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 7\end{aligned}]+20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}19 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 27\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-20)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
